host_key_mismatch.description:
The Cisco device {title} at {host} presented a different SSH host key than the one Home Assistant stored, so Home Assistant stopped connecting to it.

Stored key: `{expected}`
Presented key: `{presented}`

This is expected after you generated a new host key or replaced the device. It can also mean that another device answers on this address.

To fix this issue:
1. Check that the presented key belongs to your device: log in to the device, run `show ip ssh`, copy the key shown under `IOS Keys in SECSH format` into a file on your computer and run `ssh-keygen -l -f` on that file. The `SHA256:` fingerprint must match the presented key above. If `show ip ssh` doesn't show the key, the README of the integration explains how to use `show crypto key mypubkey rsa` instead.
2. If the new key is the one you expect, go to **Settings** > **Devices & services** > **Cisco IOS Tracker**.
3. Open the menu of the entry and select **Reconfigure**.
4. Submit the form and confirm the new host key.

After that, Home Assistant connects again and this issue is removed.
host_key_mismatch.title: SSH host key of {title} changed

import_known_devices.description: Import the devices from the `known_devices.yaml` file of the core Cisco IOS integration (or any other legacy device tracker). Each device with a MAC address gets a tracker with its old entity ID, name and icon, and is enabled if it had `track: true`. Remove the `cisco_ios` platform from your YAML configuration and restart Home Assistant first, so the old entity IDs are free.
import_known_devices.title: Import known_devices.yaml

import_known_devices_confirm.description:
Found {devices} devices with a MAC address:

- {new} get a new tracker; it shows as away until the router sees the device.
- {existing} already have a tracker, which is updated.
- {skipped} entries were skipped because they have no valid MAC address or repeat one.

Names and icons you already set in Home Assistant are kept. These entity IDs are used by another entity, so their trackers keep their current entity ID: {unavailable}.

Submit to import.
import_known_devices_confirm.title: Import known_devices.yaml

link_device.description: Show a tracker and its IP address sensor on a device from another integration, for example a Chromecast that was added without a MAC address. A link replaces the device Home Assistant picks automatically from the MAC address.

data_description.consider_home: How long, in seconds, a client stays home after it was last seen in the ARP table. With 0, a client is away as soon as a poll no longer sees it.
data_description.max_arp_age: The maximum age, in minutes, of an ARP entry for the client to count as seen. With 0, only entries that were refreshed in the last minute count. Raise this if your clients show as away while they are connected.
